import { parse } from "@21n/shared-utils/json.utils";
import {
  bundleNumber,
  iconSets,
  phIcons,
  lucideIconsForBundling,
  solarIconsForBundling
} from "@21n/ui/icons/icons-list";
import { locate } from "@iconify/json";
import { getIconData } from "@iconify/utils";
import { readFile, unlink, writeFile } from "fs/promises";

const version = bundleNumber;
const isExtension = false;

const spriteContentStart =
  '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display: none;">';

/**
 * Notes:
 * Limitation with animated svg icons via sprite. Therefore directly using svgs for svg-spinners.
 */
async function buildIconSprite() {
  let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;

  for (const setName of Object.keys(iconSets)) {
    const filename = locate(setName);
    const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      setName,
      new Set(iconSets[setName as keyof typeof iconSets])
    );
  }
  await build(spriteContent, "sprite");
}

async function buildPhSprite() {
  const filename = locate("ph");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(phIcons)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "ph",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-ph-" + key);
  }
}

async function buildLucideSprite() {
  const filename = locate("lucide");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(lucideIconsForBundling)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "lucide",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-lucide-" + key);
  }
}

async function buildSolarSprite() {
  const filename = locate("solar");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(solarIconsForBundling)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "solar",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-solar-" + key);
  }
}

async function build(spriteContent: string, prefix: string) {
  await deletePreviousVersions(prefix, version);
  spriteContent += "</svg>";
  await writeFile(resolveFullPath(prefix), spriteContent);
}

async function deletePreviousVersions(prefix: string, version: number) {
  for (let v = 1; v < version; v++) {
    try {
      await unlink(resolveFullPath(prefix, v));
      console.log(`Deleted ${prefix}-v${v}.svg`);
    } catch (error) {
      // Ignore if file doesn't exist
      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") {
        console.error(`Error deleting ${prefix}-v${v}.svg:`, error);
      }
    }
  }
}

function addIconsToSprite(
  spriteContent: string,
  set: any,
  setName: string,
  iconNames: Set<string>
) {
  for (const iconName of iconNames) {
    const iconData = getIconData(set, iconName);
    if (iconData) {
      let iconBody = iconData.body;

      if (setName === "heroicons" || setName === "mynaui") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1.2"'
        );
      }
      if (setName === "hugeicons") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1"'
        );
      }
      if (setName === "lucide") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1.2"'
        );
      }

      spriteContent += `
        <symbol id="${setName}:${iconName}" viewBox="0 0 ${iconData.width} ${iconData.height}">
          ${iconBody}
        </symbol>
      `;
    }
  }
  console.log(`${setName}: ${iconNames.size} icons added to sprite`);
  return spriteContent;
}

function resolveFullPath(prefix: string, versionParam?: number) {
  if (isExtension) {
    return `./../../../assets/icons/${prefix}.svg`;
  }
  return `./../static/icons/${prefix}-v${versionParam ?? version}.svg`;
}

buildIconSprite();
buildPhSprite();
buildLucideSprite();
buildSolarSprite();

import { parse } from "@21n/shared-utils/json.utils";
import {
  bundleNumber,
  iconSets,
  phIcons,
  lucideIconsForBundling,
  solarIconsForBundling
} from "@21n/ui/icons/icons-list";
import { locate } from "@iconify/json";
import { getIconData } from "@iconify/utils";
import { readFile, unlink, writeFile } from "fs/promises";

const version = bundleNumber;
const isExtension = false;

const spriteContentStart =
  '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display: none;">';

/**
 * Notes:
 * Limitation with animated svg icons via sprite. Therefore directly using svgs for svg-spinners.
 */
async function buildIconSprite() {
  let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;

  for (const setName of Object.keys(iconSets)) {
    const filename = locate(setName);
    const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      setName,
      new Set(iconSets[setName as keyof typeof iconSets])
    );
  }
  await build(spriteContent, "sprite");
}

async function buildPhSprite() {
  const filename = locate("ph");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(phIcons)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "ph",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-ph-" + key);
  }
}

async function buildLucideSprite() {
  const filename = locate("lucide");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(lucideIconsForBundling)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "lucide",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-lucide-" + key);
  }
}

async function buildSolarSprite() {
  const filename = locate("solar");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(solarIconsForBundling)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "solar",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-solar-" + key);
  }
}

async function build(spriteContent: string, prefix: string) {
  await deletePreviousVersions(prefix, version);
  spriteContent += "</svg>";
  await writeFile(resolveFullPath(prefix), spriteContent);
}

async function deletePreviousVersions(prefix: string, version: number) {
  for (let v = 1; v < version; v++) {
    try {
      await unlink(resolveFullPath(prefix, v));
      console.log(`Deleted ${prefix}-v${v}.svg`);
    } catch (error) {
      // Ignore if file doesn't exist
      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") {
        console.error(`Error deleting ${prefix}-v${v}.svg:`, error);
      }
    }
  }
}

function addIconsToSprite(
  spriteContent: string,
  set: any,
  setName: string,
  iconNames: Set<string>
) {
  for (const iconName of iconNames) {
    const iconData = getIconData(set, iconName);
    if (iconData) {
      let iconBody = iconData.body;

      if (setName === "heroicons" || setName === "mynaui") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1.2"'
        );
      }
      if (setName === "hugeicons") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1"'
        );
      }
      if (setName === "lucide") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1.2"'
        );
      }

      spriteContent += `
        <symbol id="${setName}:${iconName}" viewBox="0 0 ${iconData.width} ${iconData.height}">
          ${iconBody}
        </symbol>
      `;
    }
  }
  console.log(`${setName}: ${iconNames.size} icons added to sprite`);
  return spriteContent;
}

function resolveFullPath(prefix: string, versionParam?: number) {
  if (isExtension) {
    return `./../../../assets/icons/${prefix}.svg`;
  }
  return `./../static/icons/${prefix}-v${versionParam ?? version}.svg`;
}

buildIconSprite();
buildPhSprite();
buildLucideSprite();
buildSolarSprite();

import { parse } from "@21n/shared-utils/json.utils";
import {
  bundleNumber,
  iconSets,
  phIcons,
  lucideIconsForBundling,
  solarIconsForBundling
} from "@21n/ui/icons/icons-list";
import { locate } from "@iconify/json";
import { getIconData } from "@iconify/utils";
import { readFile, unlink, writeFile } from "fs/promises";

const version = bundleNumber;
const isExtension = false;

const spriteContentStart =
  '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display: none;">';

/**
 * Notes:
 * Limitation with animated svg icons via sprite. Therefore directly using svgs for svg-spinners.
 */
async function buildIconSprite() {
  let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;

  for (const setName of Object.keys(iconSets)) {
    const filename = locate(setName);
    const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      setName,
      new Set(iconSets[setName as keyof typeof iconSets])
    );
  }
  await build(spriteContent, "sprite");
}

async function buildPhSprite() {
  const filename = locate("ph");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(phIcons)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "ph",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-ph-" + key);
  }
}

async function buildLucideSprite() {
  const filename = locate("lucide");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(lucideIconsForBundling)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "lucide",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-lucide-" + key);
  }
}

async function buildSolarSprite() {
  const filename = locate("solar");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(solarIconsForBundling)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "solar",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-solar-" + key);
  }
}

async function build(spriteContent: string, prefix: string) {
  await deletePreviousVersions(prefix, version);
  spriteContent += "</svg>";
  await writeFile(resolveFullPath(prefix), spriteContent);
}

async function deletePreviousVersions(prefix: string, version: number) {
  for (let v = 1; v < version; v++) {
    try {
      await unlink(resolveFullPath(prefix, v));
      console.log(`Deleted ${prefix}-v${v}.svg`);
    } catch (error) {
      // Ignore if file doesn't exist
      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") {
        console.error(`Error deleting ${prefix}-v${v}.svg:`, error);
      }
    }
  }
}

function addIconsToSprite(
  spriteContent: string,
  set: any,
  setName: string,
  iconNames: Set<string>
) {
  for (const iconName of iconNames) {
    const iconData = getIconData(set, iconName);
    if (iconData) {
      let iconBody = iconData.body;

      if (setName === "heroicons" || setName === "mynaui") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1.2"'
        );
      }
      if (setName === "hugeicons") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1"'
        );
      }
      if (setName === "lucide") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1.2"'
        );
      }

      spriteContent += `
        <symbol id="${setName}:${iconName}" viewBox="0 0 ${iconData.width} ${iconData.height}">
          ${iconBody}
        </symbol>
      `;
    }
  }
  console.log(`${setName}: ${iconNames.size} icons added to sprite`);
  return spriteContent;
}

function resolveFullPath(prefix: string, versionParam?: number) {
  if (isExtension) {
    return `./../../../assets/icons/${prefix}.svg`;
  }
  return `./../static/icons/${prefix}-v${versionParam ?? version}.svg`;
}

buildIconSprite();
buildPhSprite();
buildLucideSprite();
buildSolarSprite();
"}

Found five actionable issues:

1. **[P1] App renames break standard dev/build commands.** [apps/nucleus/package.json:2](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/apps/nucleus/package.json:2) renames the workspace to `@nucleum/app`; Memotron and Pointron are also renamed. Root scripts still filter by the old names. Reproduced: Turbo exits with `No package found with name 'nucleus-app' in workspace`. Update all affected filters alongside the renames.

2. **[P1] Lockfile does not match the final workspace layout.** [package-lock.json:15](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/package-lock.json:15) still registers `client/capabilities` and lacks the shared-state, shell, and surfaces workspaces and links. Turbo reports missing workspaces and cannot calculate dependency closures. Deployment workflows use `npm ci`, so the lockfile needs regeneration before delivery.

3. **[P2] Playwright helpers import nonexistent modules.** [settings.spec.ts:16](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/apps/e2e-playwright/tests/shared/settings/settings.spec.ts:16) constructs imports under `client/capabilities`, although those files now live under `client/shared-state`. The same mistake affects focus session support and collection bulk-editor tests. Their browser-side dynamic imports will fail before the relevant assertions. Update all five stale paths.

4. **[P2] Link clicks invoke both host navigation and fallback navigation.** [Link.svelte:27](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/ui/elements/text/Link.svelte:27) uses `openLink(...) ?? window.open(...)`, but the configured host returns `void`. Consequently, the fallback always runs after successful host handling. An isolated execution confirmed both calls for each URL form. This duplicates navigation for enforced URLs and embedded-app links. Check host presence explicitly.

5. **[P3] Analytics charts ignore the saved font preference.** [EChart.svelte:170](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/ui/compositions/charts/EChart.svelte:170) now reads `options.typeface`, but `AnalyticsChart.svelte` never supplies it. Charts consequently use `Sen` regardless of the selected appearance font. Pass the preference from the owning feature.

Reviewed staged, unstaged, and untracked changes, including moved-file comparisons and affected callers. No branch-only commits relative to the locally recorded `origin/dev`.

Validation passed: client unit suite, all four product compiler checks, architecture checks, type ownership, and whitespace checks. Compiler warnings remain. Browser workflows, production builds, and clean installation were not run. No source or test files were edited.

# `client/application` — composition root (`@nucleum/application`)

Charter: the layer allowed to know everything and wire the product together.
Because it can import every other layer, it is the easiest place to accumulate
junk. Do not treat it as "misc".

## What legitimately lives here

1. **Composition root** — `composition/` (e.g. `resource-hosts.ts`,
   `shortcuts.config.ts`) configures every `hosts` contract and assembles the
   running product. This is the one truly app-level responsibility.
2. **Application layers** — `layers/` (base, user, auth, modal, debug) and
   `paint/` (the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`) wire the running
   product together and depend on every other layer.
3. **Modal orchestration and record presentation** — `modal/`, `record/`,
   `resource/`, `overview/`, `home/`.
4. **Chrome adapters** — `chrome/` wires the application shell's snippet slots
   (`WiredTopNav.svelte`, `WiredLeftNav.svelte`) with surfaces, product
   branding, and application chrome providers.
5. **App-specific integrations** — `embed/`, `network/`, `maps/`, `taco/`,
   `share/`, `branding/` (product-aware adapters), plus dev-only `debug/`,
   `cx/`, `storybook/` pending their own homes.

## What moved out

- The application shell (navigation, panels, split views, tabs, overlays,
  layers) is the top-level `client/shell/` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`).
- Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help,
  settings, command, search, library) are the top-level `client/surfaces/`
  workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). `features/` must never import surfaces
  (enforced).

## Never add here

- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome -> `shell/`.
- A cross-feature product surface -> `surfaces/`.
- A content capability -> `features/`.
- Portable, domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Shared cross-feature state -> `shared-state/`.
- Transport / native / inference infrastructure -> `runtime/`.

## Junk-drawer test

Before adding a folder here, name which of the three kinds above it is. If it is
none, it does not belong in `application`.
# `client/surfaces` — cross-feature product surfaces (`@nucleum/surfaces`)

Charter: user-facing surfaces that are about the app itself or operate across
all content features. Second-order UI: it composes `features/`, `shell/`, and
shared state into product-level experiences.

## Owners

`account` (identity workflows), `subscription` (billing), `onboarding`, `help`,
`settings`, `commandBar` + `commands` + `search` (command surface), `library`
(resource browsing and rendering).

## Why not `features/`

Features are first-order content capabilities a user creates and manages
(memory, focus, collections, spaces, calendar). Surfaces are about the product:
identity, billing, settings, command dispatch, and browsing every resource type.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `features`, `shell`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, `ui`,
  `products`, and `application` composition.
- `features/` must never import `surfaces/` — this edge is rejected by
  `npm run check:architecture`.

## Junk-drawer test

- A first-order content capability? -> `features/`.
- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome? -> `shell/`.
- Product wiring (host-contract configuration, base layers)? -> `application`
  composition.
- Dev-only tooling? -> `tools/` or delete, never here.
# `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`)

Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content
fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does".

## Owners

`navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`,
`leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, sync, metadata, embed,
analytics, cache, support chrome), `overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and
resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`,
`tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome.

## Belongs here

Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product
menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen
does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here.

## Not here

- Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) ->
  `surfaces/`.
- Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Content capabilities -> `features/`.
- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
  settings action map) -> `application/`.

## Dependency direction (enforced)

Shell is acyclic: it must not import `application/`, `surfaces/`, or
`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
`@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome
(brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status,
capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props provided
by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).

## Junk-drawer test

A shell component may read navigation and shell state, but it must not contain a
feature workflow. If it orchestrates a domain task (sign-in, billing, resource
browsing), it is a surface, not shell.
# `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`)

Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a
self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry
points.

## Owners

`calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`, `system`.

## Belongs here

A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application
  **shell** surface only.
- May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell.
- Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in
  `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel.

## Junk-drawer test

If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account
and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings,
onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level
`client/surfaces/` workspace (see `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md`).
`features/` must never import `surfaces/`; the checker rejects that edge.

# `client/application` — composition root (`@nucleum/application`)

Charter: the layer allowed to know everything and wire the product together.
Because it can import every other layer, it is the easiest place to accumulate
junk. Do not treat it as "misc".

## What legitimately lives here

1. **Composition root** — `composition/` (e.g. `resource-hosts.ts`,
   `shortcuts.config.ts`) configures every `hosts` contract and assembles the
   running product. This is the one truly app-level responsibility.
2. **Application layers** — `layers/` (base, user, auth, modal, debug) and
   `paint/` (the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`) wire the running
   product together and depend on every other layer.
3. **Modal orchestration and record presentation** — `modal/`, `record/`,
   `resource/`, `overview/`, `home/`.
4. **Chrome adapters** — `chrome/` wires the application shell's snippet slots
   (`WiredTopNav.svelte`, `WiredLeftNav.svelte`) with surfaces, product
   branding, and application chrome providers.
5. **App-specific integrations** — `embed/`, `network/`, `maps/`, `taco/`,
   `share/`, `branding/` (product-aware adapters), plus dev-only `debug/`,
   `cx/`, `storybook/` pending their own homes.

## What moved out

- The application shell (navigation, panels, split views, tabs, overlays,
  layers) is the top-level `client/shell/` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`).
- Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help,
  settings, command, search, library) are the top-level `client/surfaces/`
  workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). `features/` must never import surfaces
  (enforced).

## Never add here

- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome -> `shell/`.
- A cross-feature product surface -> `surfaces/`.
- A content capability -> `features/`.
- Portable, domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Shared cross-feature state -> `shared-state/`.
- Transport / native / inference infrastructure -> `runtime/`.

## Junk-drawer test

Before adding a folder here, name which of the three kinds above it is. If it is
none, it does not belong in `application`.
# `client/surfaces` — cross-feature product surfaces (`@nucleum/surfaces`)

Charter: user-facing surfaces that are about the app itself or operate across
all content features. Second-order UI: it composes `features/`, `shell/`, and
shared state into product-level experiences.

## Owners

`account` (identity workflows), `subscription` (billing), `onboarding`, `help`,
`settings`, `commandBar` + `commands` + `search` (command surface), `library`
(resource browsing and rendering).

## Why not `features/`

Features are first-order content capabilities a user creates and manages
(memory, focus, collections, spaces, calendar). Surfaces are about the product:
identity, billing, settings, command dispatch, and browsing every resource type.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `features`, `shell`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, `ui`,
  `products`, and `application` composition.
- `features/` must never import `surfaces/` — this edge is rejected by
  `npm run check:architecture`.

## Junk-drawer test

- A first-order content capability? -> `features/`.
- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome? -> `shell/`.
- Product wiring (host-contract configuration, base layers)? -> `application`
  composition.
- Dev-only tooling? -> `tools/` or delete, never here.
# `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`)

Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content
fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does".

## Owners

`navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`,
`leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, sync, metadata, embed,
analytics, cache, support chrome), `overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and
resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`,
`tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome.

## Belongs here

Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product
menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen
does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here.

## Not here

- Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) ->
  `surfaces/`.
- Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Content capabilities -> `features/`.
- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
  settings action map) -> `application/`.

## Dependency direction (enforced)

Shell is acyclic: it must not import `application/`, `surfaces/`, or
`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
`@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome
(brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status,
capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props provided
by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).

## Junk-drawer test

A shell component may read navigation and shell state, but it must not contain a
feature workflow. If it orchestrates a domain task (sign-in, billing, resource
browsing), it is a surface, not shell.
# `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`)

Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a
self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry
points.

## Owners

`calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`, `system`.

## Belongs here

A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application
  **shell** surface only.
- May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell.
- Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in
  `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel.

## Junk-drawer test

If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account
and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings,
onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level
`client/surfaces/` workspace (see `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md`).
`features/` must never import `surfaces/`; the checker rejects that edge.

# `client/application` — composition root (`@nucleum/application`)

Charter: the layer allowed to know everything and wire the product together.
Because it can import every other layer, it is the easiest place to accumulate
junk. Do not treat it as "misc".

## What legitimately lives here

1. **Composition root** — `composition/` (e.g. `resource-hosts.ts`,
   `shortcuts.config.ts`) configures every `hosts` contract and assembles the
   running product. This is the one truly app-level responsibility.
2. **Application layers** — `layers/` (base, user, auth, modal, debug) and
   `paint/` (the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`) wire the running
   product together and depend on every other layer.
3. **Modal orchestration and record presentation** — `modal/`, `record/`,
   `resource/`, `overview/`, `home/`.
4. **Chrome adapters** — `chrome/` wires the application shell's snippet slots
   (`WiredTopNav.svelte`, `WiredLeftNav.svelte`) with surfaces, product
   branding, and application chrome providers.
5. **App-specific integrations** — `embed/`, `network/`, `maps/`, `taco/`,
   `share/`, `branding/` (product-aware adapters), plus dev-only `debug/`,
   `cx/`, `storybook/` pending their own homes.

## What moved out

- The application shell (navigation, panels, split views, tabs, overlays,
  layers) is the top-level `client/shell/` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`).
- Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help,
  settings, command, search, library) are the top-level `client/surfaces/`
  workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). `features/` must never import surfaces
  (enforced).

## Never add here

- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome -> `shell/`.
- A cross-feature product surface -> `surfaces/`.
- A content capability -> `features/`.
- Portable, domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Shared cross-feature state -> `shared-state/`.
- Transport / native / inference infrastructure -> `runtime/`.

## Junk-drawer test

Before adding a folder here, name which of the three kinds above it is. If it is
none, it does not belong in `application`.
# `client/surfaces` — cross-feature product surfaces (`@nucleum/surfaces`)

Charter: user-facing surfaces that are about the app itself or operate across
all content features. Second-order UI: it composes `features/`, `shell/`, and
shared state into product-level experiences.

## Owners

`account` (identity workflows), `subscription` (billing), `onboarding`, `help`,
`settings`, `commandBar` + `commands` + `search` (command surface), `library`
(resource browsing and rendering).

## Why not `features/`

Features are first-order content capabilities a user creates and manages
(memory, focus, collections, spaces, calendar). Surfaces are about the product:
identity, billing, settings, command dispatch, and browsing every resource type.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `features`, `shell`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, `ui`,
  `products`, and `application` composition.
- `features/` must never import `surfaces/` — this edge is rejected by
  `npm run check:architecture`.

## Junk-drawer test

- A first-order content capability? -> `features/`.
- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome? -> `shell/`.
- Product wiring (host-contract configuration, base layers)? -> `application`
  composition.
- Dev-only tooling? -> `tools/` or delete, never here.
# `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`)

Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content
fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does".

## Owners

`navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`,
`leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, sync, metadata, embed,
analytics, cache, support chrome), `overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and
resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`,
`tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome.

## Belongs here

Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product
menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen
does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here.

## Not here

- Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) ->
  `surfaces/`.
- Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Content capabilities -> `features/`.
- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
  settings action map) -> `application/`.

## Dependency direction (enforced)

Shell is acyclic: it must not import `application/`, `surfaces/`, or
`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
`@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome
(brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status,
capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props provided
by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).

## Junk-drawer test

A shell component may read navigation and shell state, but it must not contain a
feature workflow. If it orchestrates a domain task (sign-in, billing, resource
browsing), it is a surface, not shell.
# `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`)

Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a
self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry
points.

## Owners

`calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`, `system`.

## Belongs here

A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application
  **shell** surface only.
- May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell.
- Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in
  `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel.

## Junk-drawer test

If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account
and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings,
onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level
`client/surfaces/` workspace (see `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md`).
`features/` must never import `surfaces/`; the checker rejects that edge.

47:Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.
49:`client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively. Consumers import named subpaths such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`; there is no root barrel, `shared`, `core`, generic `state`, or nested generic `stores` bucket.
51:Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary.
53:Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.
57:Registered workspaces declare their production source imports. `@nucleum/client` owns lower-level config and runtime; `@nucleum/shared-state` owns product-independent shared client behavior, application context, command ports, and events; `@nucleum/shell` owns the application shell; `@nucleum/surfaces` owns cross-feature product surfaces; `@21n/ui` owns all portable presentation and visual assets. Source workspaces bundled by an app declare co-hosted workspace requirements as peer dependencies; existing build dependencies remain dependencies. Peers describe the host's source compilation requirements without adding artificial Turbo build cycles. This is not a claim that each source package builds or installs independently. The checker verifies both resolved workspace and external package imports; test and story dependencies are outside this production-source check.

63:Product and application context lives in `client/shared-state/app-context/app.store.ts`. Browser/embed environment context lives in `client/runtime/context.store.ts`; persistent UI preference state lives in `client/shared-state/preferences/ui-state`; legacy product-key migration belongs to `client/persistence/migrations`. URL/history and resource navigation live in `client/shell/navigation/navigation.ts`. Product command lookup/execution lives in `client/surfaces/commands/action-runner.ts`; the permanent shared `CommandHost` contract lives in `client/shared-state/commands/command-host.ts` and is installed from `resource-hosts.ts`. Application-wide events live in `client/shared-state/events`. No old methods delegate to the new owners.
65:Reactive account session state lives with the account runtime in `client/runtime/account/account.store.ts`. Authentication persistence, bootstrap, sign-in, sign-out, navigation, and DataFn teardown are coordinated by `client/surfaces/account/account-session.ts`. Deletion confirmation and cleanup orchestration live in `client/surfaces/account/account-deletion.ts`; subscription operations live in `client/surfaces/subscription/subscription.ts`; file conversion, thumbnail generation, signing, and local/remote storage live in `client/shared-state/files/file-upload.ts`. Legacy OAuth initiation belongs to application account composition.
67:The connected offline-status indicator lives with sync settings in `client/surfaces/settings/sync`; shared elements do not read account session state. Application and product shells consume the application-owned indicator directly.
69:Product menu persistence lives beside navigation. Tab and sidebar mutations live beside the application shell; generic UI-state persistence belongs to the preferences capability. Shortcut persistence, matching, hints, and the host contract live in `client/shared-state/shortcuts`; global shortcut execution lives in `client/shell/shortcuts`, and shortcut settings presentation lives in `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Headless notification state lives in `client/shared-state/notifications`, while connected notification rendering lives in `client/shell/notifications`. Focus owns its scheduled notification queue, and the existing native transport delivers messages. Memory owns its word-count and PDF-overlay DOM actions. The unused Markdown action and empty `@nucleum/cx` workspace are retired, including active aliases and workspace declarations.

Runtime environment state belongs to runtime, migration state belongs to persistence, the observable-store implementation belongs to DataFn, and overlay state belongs to the application shell. The standalone `@21n/icons` and `@21n/icons-v2` workspaces are retired.

The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired.

A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, modal orchestration, record presentation, app-specific integrations, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory.
34:- Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition; the top-level shell is the only app-level layer features may consume. Surfaces may compose features; features must never import surfaces.
35:- The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).
36:- Portable UI cannot directly or transitively import application state, runtime, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state.
38:- Shared state cannot directly or transitively import application, feature, or product implementations.
39:- DataFn and runtime files cannot directly import features, products, application composition or shell, portable UI, or shared client state and services.
45:## Current architecture contract
47:Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.
49:`client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively. Consumers import named subpaths such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`; there is no root barrel, `shared`, `core`, generic `state`, or nested generic `stores` bucket.
51:Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary.
53:Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.
57:Registered workspaces declare their production source imports. `@nucleum/client` owns lower-level config and runtime; `@nucleum/shared-state` owns product-independent shared client behavior, application context, command ports, and events; `@nucleum/shell` owns the application shell; `@nucleum/surfaces` owns cross-feature product surfaces; `@21n/ui` owns all portable presentation and visual assets. Source workspaces bundled by an app declare co-hosted workspace requirements as peer dependencies; existing build dependencies remain dependencies. Peers describe the host's source compilation requirements without adding artificial Turbo build cycles. This is not a claim that each source package builds or installs independently. The checker verifies both resolved workspace and external package imports; test and story dependencies are outside this production-source check.
61:## Application-state ownership follow-up
63:Product and application context lives in `client/shared-state/app-context/app.store.ts`. Browser/embed environment context lives in `client/runtime/context.store.ts`; persistent UI preference state lives in `client/shared-state/preferences/ui-state`; legacy product-key migration belongs to `client/persistence/migrations`. URL/history and resource navigation live in `client/shell/navigation/navigation.ts`. Product command lookup/execution lives in `client/surfaces/commands/action-runner.ts`; the permanent shared `CommandHost` contract lives in `client/shared-state/commands/command-host.ts` and is installed from `resource-hosts.ts`. Application-wide events live in `client/shared-state/events`. No old methods delegate to the new owners.
65:Reactive account session state lives with the account runtime in `client/runtime/account/account.store.ts`. Authentication persistence, bootstrap, sign-in, sign-out, navigation, and DataFn teardown are coordinated by `client/surfaces/account/account-session.ts`. Deletion confirmation and cleanup orchestration live in `client/surfaces/account/account-deletion.ts`; subscription operations live in `client/surfaces/subscription/subscription.ts`; file conversion, thumbnail generation, signing, and local/remote storage live in `client/shared-state/files/file-upload.ts`. Legacy OAuth initiation belongs to application account composition.
67:The connected offline-status indicator lives with sync settings in `client/surfaces/settings/sync`; shared elements do not read account session state. Application and product shells consume the application-owned indicator directly.
69:Product menu persistence lives beside navigation. Tab and sidebar mutations live beside the application shell; generic UI-state persistence belongs to the preferences capability. Shortcut persistence, matching, hints, and the host contract live in `client/shared-state/shortcuts`; global shortcut execution lives in `client/shell/shortcuts`, and shortcut settings presentation lives in `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Headless notification state lives in `client/shared-state/notifications`, while connected notification rendering lives in `client/shell/notifications`. Focus owns its scheduled notification queue, and the existing native transport delivers messages. Memory owns its word-count and PDF-overlay DOM actions. The unused Markdown action and empty `@nucleum/cx` workspace are retired, including active aliases and workspace declarations.
71:The former `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, and `client/events` directories are retired. App context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts have explicit owners under `client/shared-state`. Runtime environment state belongs to runtime, migration state belongs to persistence, the observable-store implementation belongs to DataFn, and overlay state belongs to the application shell. New state follows semantic ownership and must not recreate a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory; `client/shared-state` is the single approved shared-state workspace and keeps named owners with no root barrel.
75:Portable legacy SVG/Rive icons, generated icon mappings, sprite resolution, and spinner components live under `client/ui/icons` and are imported through `@21n/ui/icons/*`. The UI package never imports the product static package; the application supplies asset URL resolution through the UI environment contract. The standalone `@21n/icons` and `@21n/icons-v2` workspaces are retired.
77:Portable illustrations live under `client/ui/illustrations`, and pure product/provider marks live under `client/ui/branding`. The product-aware `SubAtomLogo` adapter remains under `client/application/branding` because it reads product persistence and composes the portable marks. The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired.
79:The concrete layout package is the top-level `client/shell` workspace. All callers use `@nucleum/shell/*`; the `@21n/layout` package, alias, workspace, and compatibility paths are retired. Features may use the shell's explicit navigation, overlay, and shell-presentation surface when participating in application composition, while imports from surfaces or application composition remain forbidden.
"}

import { parse } from "@21n/shared-utils/json.utils";
import {
  bundleNumber,
  iconSets,
  phIcons,
  lucideIconsForBundling,
  solarIconsForBundling
} from "@21n/ui/icons/icons-list";
import { locate } from "@iconify/json";
import { getIconData } from "@iconify/utils";
import { readFile, unlink, writeFile } from "fs/promises";

const version = bundleNumber;
const isExtension = false;

const spriteContentStart =
  '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" style="display: none;">';

/**
 * Notes:
 * Limitation with animated svg icons via sprite. Therefore directly using svgs for svg-spinners.
 */
async function buildIconSprite() {
  let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;

  for (const setName of Object.keys(iconSets)) {
    const filename = locate(setName);
    const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      setName,
      new Set(iconSets[setName as keyof typeof iconSets])
    );
  }
  await build(spriteContent, "sprite");
}

async function buildPhSprite() {
  const filename = locate("ph");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(phIcons)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "ph",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-ph-" + key);
  }
}

async function buildLucideSprite() {
  const filename = locate("lucide");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(lucideIconsForBundling)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "lucide",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-lucide-" + key);
  }
}

async function buildSolarSprite() {
  const filename = locate("solar");
  const icons = parse(await readFile(filename, "utf8"));
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(solarIconsForBundling)) {
    let spriteContent = spriteContentStart;
    spriteContent = addIconsToSprite(
      spriteContent,
      icons,
      "solar",
      new Set(value)
    );
    await build(spriteContent, "sprite-solar-" + key);
  }
}

async function build(spriteContent: string, prefix: string) {
  await deletePreviousVersions(prefix, version);
  spriteContent += "</svg>";
  await writeFile(resolveFullPath(prefix), spriteContent);
}

async function deletePreviousVersions(prefix: string, version: number) {
  for (let v = 1; v < version; v++) {
    try {
      await unlink(resolveFullPath(prefix, v));
      console.log(`Deleted ${prefix}-v${v}.svg`);
    } catch (error) {
      // Ignore if file doesn't exist
      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") {
        console.error(`Error deleting ${prefix}-v${v}.svg:`, error);
      }
    }
  }
}

function addIconsToSprite(
  spriteContent: string,
  set: any,
  setName: string,
  iconNames: Set<string>
) {
  for (const iconName of iconNames) {
    const iconData = getIconData(set, iconName);
    if (iconData) {
      let iconBody = iconData.body;

      if (setName === "heroicons" || setName === "mynaui") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1.2"'
        );
      }
      if (setName === "hugeicons") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1"'
        );
      }
      if (setName === "lucide") {
        iconBody = iconBody.replace(
          /stroke-width="[^"]*"/g,
          'stroke-width="1.2"'
        );
      }

      spriteContent += `
        <symbol id="${setName}:${iconName}" viewBox="0 0 ${iconData.width} ${iconData.height}">
          ${iconBody}
        </symbol>
      `;
    }
  }
  console.log(`${setName}: ${iconNames.size} icons added to sprite`);
  return spriteContent;
}

function resolveFullPath(prefix: string, versionParam?: number) {
  if (isExtension) {
    return `./../../../assets/icons/${prefix}.svg`;
  }
  return `./../static/icons/${prefix}-v${versionParam ?? version}.svg`;
}

buildIconSprite();
buildPhSprite();
buildLucideSprite();
buildSolarSprite();
"}

content.text:
Found five actionable issues:

1. **[P1] App renames break standard dev/build commands.** [apps/nucleus/package.json:2](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/apps/nucleus/package.json:2) renames the workspace to `@nucleum/app`; Memotron and Pointron are also renamed. Root scripts still filter by the old names. Reproduced: Turbo exits with `No package found with name 'nucleus-app' in workspace`. Update all affected filters alongside the renames.

2. **[P1] Lockfile does not match the final workspace layout.** [package-lock.json:15](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/package-lock.json:15) still registers `client/capabilities` and lacks the shared-state, shell, and surfaces workspaces and links. Turbo reports missing workspaces and cannot calculate dependency closures. Deployment workflows use `npm ci`, so the lockfile needs regeneration before delivery.

3. **[P2] Playwright helpers import nonexistent modules.** [settings.spec.ts:16](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/apps/e2e-playwright/tests/shared/settings/settings.spec.ts:16) constructs imports under `client/capabilities`, although those files now live under `client/shared-state`. The same mistake affects focus session support and collection bulk-editor tests. Their browser-side dynamic imports will fail before the relevant assertions. Update all five stale paths.

4. **[P2] Link clicks invoke both host navigation and fallback navigation.** [Link.svelte:27](/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/nucleus/client/ui/elements/text/Link.svelte:27) uses `openLink(...) ?? window.open(...)`, but the configured host returns `void`. # `client/application` — composition root (`@nucleum/application`)

Charter: the layer allowed to know everything and wire the product together.
Because it can import every other layer, it is the easiest place to accumulate
junk. Do not treat it as "misc".

## What legitimately lives here

1. **Composition root** — `composition/` (e.g. `resource-hosts.ts`,
   `shortcuts.config.ts`) configures every `hosts` contract and assembles the
   running product. This is the one truly app-level responsibility.
2. **Application layers** — `layers/` (base, user, auth, modal, debug) and
   `paint/` (the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`) wire the running
   product together and depend on every other layer.
3. **Modal orchestration and record presentation** — `modal/`, `record/`,
   `resource/`, `overview/`, `home/`.
4. **Chrome adapters** — `chrome/` wires the application shell's snippet slots
   (`WiredTopNav.svelte`, `WiredLeftNav.svelte`) with surfaces, product
   branding, and application chrome providers.
5. **App-specific integrations** — `embed/`, `network/`, `maps/`, `taco/`,
   `share/`, `branding/` (product-aware adapters), plus dev-only `debug/`,
   `cx/`, `storybook/` pending their own homes.

## What moved out

- The application shell (navigation, panels, split views, tabs, overlays,
  layers) is the top-level `client/shell/` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`).
- Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help,
  settings, command, search, library) are the top-level `client/surfaces/`
  workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). `features/` must never import surfaces
  (enforced).

## Never add here

- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome -> `shell/`.
- A cross-feature product surface -> `surfaces/`.
- A content capability -> `features/`.
- Portable, domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Shared cross-feature state -> `shared-state/`.
- Transport / native / inference infrastructure -> `runtime/`.

## Junk-drawer test

Before adding a folder here, name which of the three kinds above it is. If it is
none, it does not belong in `application`.
# `client/surfaces` — cross-feature product surfaces (`@nucleum/surfaces`)

Charter: user-facing surfaces that are about the app itself or operate across
all content features. Second-order UI: it composes `features/`, `shell/`, and
shared state into product-level experiences.

## Owners

`account` (identity workflows), `subscription` (billing), `onboarding`, `help`,
`settings`, `commandBar` + `commands` + `search` (command surface), `library`
(resource browsing and rendering).

## Why not `features/`

Features are first-order content capabilities a user creates and manages
(memory, focus, collections, spaces, calendar). Surfaces are about the product:
identity, billing, settings, command dispatch, and browsing every resource type.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `features`, `shell`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, `ui`,
  `products`, and `application` composition.
- `features/` must never import `surfaces/` — this edge is rejected by
  `npm run check:architecture`.

## Junk-drawer test

- A first-order content capability? -> `features/`.
- Pure arrangement/navigation chrome? -> `shell/`.
- Product wiring (host-contract configuration, base layers)? -> `application`
  composition.
- Dev-only tooling? -> `tools/` or delete, never here.
# `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`)

Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content
fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does".

## Owners

`navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`,
`leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, sync, metadata, embed,
analytics, cache, support chrome), `overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and
resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`,
`tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome.

## Belongs here

Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product
menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen
does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here.

## Not here

- Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) ->
  `surfaces/`.
- Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Content capabilities -> `features/`.
- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
  settings action map) -> `application/`.

## Dependency direction (enforced)

Shell is acyclic: it must not import `application/`, `surfaces/`, or
`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
`@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome
(brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status,
capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props provided
by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).

## Junk-drawer test

A shell component may read navigation and shell state, but it must not contain a
feature workflow. If it orchestrates a domain task (sign-in, billing, resource
browsing), it is a surface, not shell.
# `client/features` — user-facing content capabilities (`@nucleum/features`)

Charter: the marquee things a user creates and manages. Each feature is a
self-contained capability reached from outside only through declared entry
points.

## Owners

`calendar`, `collections`, `focus`, `memory`, `records`, `spaces`, `system`.

## Belongs here

A cohesive content capability with its own UI, state, and logic.

## Import rules (enforced)

- May import `ui`, `shared-state`, `runtime`, `datafn`, and the application
  **shell** surface only.
- May **not** import `products` or application workflows outside the shell.
- Cross-feature imports must target a path declared in
  `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`; there is no barrel.

## Junk-drawer test

If the thing operates *across* features or is *about the app itself* — account
and billing, the command palette, the resource library/browser, settings,
onboarding, help — it is a **product surface** and belongs in the top-level
`client/surfaces/` workspace (see `docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md`).
`features/` must never import `surfaces/`; the checker rejects that edge.

45:## Current architecture contract
47:Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic.
49:`client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively. Consumers import named subpaths such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`; there is no root barrel, `shared`, `core`, generic `state`, or nested generic `stores` bucket.
51:Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary.
53:Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations.
57:Registered workspaces declare their production source imports. `@nucleum/client` owns lower-level config and runtime; `@nucleum/shared-state` owns product-independent shared client behavior, application context, command ports, and events; `@nucleum/shell` owns the application shell; `@nucleum/surfaces` owns cross-feature product surfaces; `@21n/ui` owns all portable presentation and visual assets. Source workspaces bundled by an app declare co-hosted workspace requirements as peer dependencies; existing build dependencies remain dependencies. Peers describe the host's source compilation requirements without adding artificial Turbo build cycles. This is not a claim that each source package builds or installs independently. The checker verifies both resolved workspace and external package imports; test and story dependencies are outside this production-source check.
61:## Application-state ownership follow-up
63:Product and application context lives in `client/shared-state/app-context/app.store.ts`. Browser/embed environment context lives in `client/runtime/context.store.ts`; persistent UI preference state lives in `client/shared-state/preferences/ui-state`; legacy product-key migration belongs to `client/persistence/migrations`. URL/history and resource navigation live in `client/shell/navigation/navigation.ts`. Product command lookup/execution lives in `client/surfaces/commands/action-runner.ts`; the permanent shared `CommandHost` contract lives in `client/shared-state/commands/command-host.ts` and is installed from `resource-hosts.ts`. Application-wide events live in `client/shared-state/events`. No old methods delegate to the new owners.
65:Reactive account session state lives with the account runtime in `client/runtime/account/account.store.ts`. Authentication persistence, bootstrap, sign-in, sign-out, navigation, and DataFn teardown are coordinated by `client/surfaces/account/account-session.ts`. Deletion confirmation and cleanup orchestration live in `client/surfaces/account/account-deletion.ts`; subscription operations live in `client/surfaces/subscription/subscription.ts`; file conversion, thumbnail generation, signing, and local/remote storage live in `client/shared-state/files/file-upload.ts`. Legacy OAuth initiation belongs to application account composition.
67:The connected offline-status indicator lives with sync settings in `client/surfaces/settings/sync`; shared elements do not read account session state. Application and product shells consume the application-owned indicator directly.
69:Product menu persistence lives beside navigation. Tab and sidebar mutations live beside the application shell; generic UI-state persistence belongs to the preferences capability. Shortcut persistence, matching, hints, and the host contract live in `client/shared-state/shortcuts`; global shortcut execution lives in `client/shell/shortcuts`, and shortcut settings presentation lives in `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Headless notification state lives in `client/shared-state/notifications`, while connected notification rendering lives in `client/shell/notifications`. Focus owns its scheduled notification queue, and the existing native transport delivers messages. Memory owns its word-count and PDF-overlay DOM actions. The unused Markdown action and empty `@nucleum/cx` workspace are retired, including active aliases and workspace declarations.
71:The former `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, and `client/events` directories are retired. App context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts have explicit owners under `client/shared-state`. Runtime environment state belongs to runtime, migration state belongs to persistence, the observable-store implementation belongs to DataFn, and overlay state belongs to the application shell. New state follows semantic ownership and must not recreate a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory; `client/shared-state` is the single approved shared-state workspace and keeps named owners with no root barrel.
75:Portable legacy SVG/Rive icons, generated icon mappings, sprite resolution, and spinner components live under `client/ui/icons` and are imported through `@21n/ui/icons/*`. The UI package never imports the product static package; the application supplies asset URL resolution through the UI environment contract. The standalone `@21n/icons` and `@21n/icons-v2` workspaces are retired.
77:Portable illustrations live under `client/ui/illustrations`, and pure product/provider marks live under `client/ui/branding`. The product-aware `SubAtomLogo` adapter remains under `client/application/branding` because it reads product persistence and composes the portable marks. The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired.
79:The concrete layout package is the top-level `client/shell` workspace. All callers use `@nucleum/shell/*`; the `@21n/layout` package, alias, workspace, and compatibility paths are retired. Features may use the shell's explicit navigation, overlay, and shell-presentation surface when participating in application composition, while imports from surfaces or application composition remain forbidden.
