# Applications | App | Website | Description | | -------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Memotron | [memotron.app](https://memotron.app) | **Your memory atlas**, a tool for managing your digital memory and personal knowledge.

Tags: Digital memory, PKM, Note‑taking, Knowledge management. | | Pointron | [pointron.app](https://pointron.app) | **Your focus haven**, a tool for tracking your goals and managing your time.

Tags: Focus, Time tracking, Goals, Events and Task management. | *For early access to our new products - please join our Discord [here](https://discord.com/invite/9HJqKYTZKg). **Note:** All of the above tools are designed for personal use and lack team/group features like collaboration, sharing, etc. # Self hosting Currently, only the frontend apps can be self‑hosted on your own server. This means you cannot sync data between devices when self‑hosting. To deploy the offline‑only frontend at your own URL, follow these steps. 1. Clone/Fork this repository 2. This is a turbo repo with `/apps` folder containing apps that can be deployed. Choose the app sub-folder corresponding to the app you want to run. 3. Set the environment variables. 4. Deploy to the provider of your choice ```env VITE_PRODUCT={{memotron | pointron | nucleum }} VITE_STATIC_URL=https://cdn.21n.co ``` _Full app deployment including backend will be available soon..._ ## Contributing Due to the current size of our team, we are not accepting external contributions at this time. We appreciate your interest and understanding. ### License This project is licensed under the AGPL-3.0 license. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details. ### Contact For any questions, security reporting or feedback, please contact us at [hello@21n.co](mailto:hello@21n.co). ❤️ We extend our deepest gratitude to all the [OSS libraries and tools](https://github.com/21nOrg/nucleus/network/dependencies) that made this project possible. ## Code organization Product bundles in `apps/` compose user-facing features from `client/features/`. `client/ui/` is the domain-free, portable `@21n/ui` package: `elements` owns atomic controls, `compositions` owns reusable compound UI such as charts, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, and time controls, `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, `branding` owns pure visual brand assets, and `environment` plus `hosts` provide package-wide integration contracts. Portable UI receives product behavior through props or narrow hosts and remains independent of application state, runtime infrastructure, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Product-independent Nucleum behavior shared across features or products lives in named subdirectories of `client/capabilities/` and is imported from `@nucleum/capabilities/*`, including command ports and application events; this package must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. `schema/` owns cross-layer contracts, `client/datafn/` owns storage and sync, and `services/account/` owns the backend. Application workflows and the concrete shell live in `client/application/`, including navigation, notification presentation, and shortcut execution under `client/application/shell`; UI-independent infrastructure lives in `client/runtime/`. State is colocated with app context, runtime, preferences, persistence, shell, or feature owners rather than a generic `client/state` directory. See [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md) for the current ownership model, [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md) for contracts, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for maintainer orientation. # Contributor and maintainer orientation As noted in README.md, external contributions are not currently accepted. This guide documents the workflow for maintainers and authorized agents. Start with [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [WARP.md](WARP.md), [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md), and [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md). Confirm the active product in `client/products` and `client/config`. Reuse `@21n/ui/elements` for atomic controls, `@21n/ui/compositions` for portable domain-neutral compound UI, `@21n/ui/actions` for generic DOM behavior, `@21n/ui/icons` for portable icons, `@21n/ui/illustrations` for artwork, and `@21n/ui/branding` for pure visual brand assets. UI-wide platform state and dependency-inversion contracts belong to `@21n/ui/environment` and `@21n/ui/hosts`, not under an individual element. Keep a composition shared when credible future reuse is intentional even if it currently has one consumer. The entire UI package must remain independent of application state, runtime, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state; inject product behavior through props or narrow host contracts. Keep product-aware branding and other connected adapters with application composition. The concrete application shell lives under `client/application/shell`; the generic `client/layout`, `client/branding`, `client/illustrations`, `client/icons`, `client/iconsV2`, `client/commands`, `client/events`, and `client/state` owners are retired. Product-independent app-context, appearance, command, event, file, notification, preference, resource, and shortcut behavior belongs to named `@nucleum/capabilities/*` subpaths, which must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. Connected notification rendering and shortcut execution belong to the shell, while shortcut settings UI belongs under `client/application/settings/shortcuts`. Use repository scripts for setup, compilation, tests, and builds. Run architecture and type-ownership checks for moves, and include a forward migration when generated database mappings change. Do not modify existing tests without the per-file authorization required by AGENTS.md. PRs should describe the user-visible result, ownership changes, checks performed, and limitations. Do not include secrets, local environment files, build output, or unrelated workspace changes. # Repository guide `AGENTS.md` is the governing agent policy. Read it before changes. The current architecture is documented in [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md) and [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md). ## Organization - `schema/`: cross-layer product/resource definitions, wire contracts, and legacy serialization contracts. - `client/datafn/`: client storage, queries, sync, and DataFn resource adapters. - `client/runtime/`: UI-independent auth/account transport, connectivity, logging, native messaging, audio, and inference. - `client/features/`: shared capabilities such as memory, focus, calendar, collections, and spaces. - `client/products/`: product-specific composition, configuration, and integrations. - `client/config/`: client product identity, navigation metadata, and command identifiers. - `client/application/`: commands, account/subscription workflows, settings, mixed-resource presentation, and the concrete shell under `client/application/shell`. - `client/ui/`: the domain-free `@21n/ui` package. Import atomic controls from `@21n/ui/elements`, reusable compound UI from `@21n/ui/compositions`, generic DOM behavior from `@21n/ui/actions`, portable icons from `@21n/ui/icons`, illustrations from `@21n/ui/illustrations`, pure visual brand assets from `@21n/ui/branding`, portable platform state from `@21n/ui/environment`, and host contracts from `@21n/ui/hosts`. - `client/capabilities/`: the product-independent `@nucleum/capabilities` package with named app-context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts owners. - `client/persistence/`: persistence helpers and legacy backup/recovery boundaries. - `services/account/`: AuthFn/DataFn account service, database mappings, lookup integrations, and Node/Worker deployments. - `shared/`: cross-layer utilities and remaining legacy database objects. - `apps/`, `extensions/`: deployable product and extension bundles; `apps/e2e-playwright` owns browser verification. There is no global `client/types` or `shared/types` package. Import contracts from their domain owner. The unused `@nucleum/cx` workspace is retired. ## Composition rules App context does not implement navigation or command execution. The command capability exposes the application port; the application command runner executes product commands. The application shell changes URL/history and owns connected notification rendering plus global shortcut execution. Shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/application/settings/shortcuts`. Application and extension shells install command, overlay, resource, renderer, shortcut, recents, icon-asset, and UI-environment hosts through `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` before mounting consumers. Compositions may use elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers must not depend on compositions. Nothing under `client/ui` may directly or transitively depend on application state, runtime, shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state. Supply connected behavior through props or narrow host contracts and keep the adapter with its application, shell, or feature owner. Product-aware branding is an application adapter over portable brand assets. Do not move a domain-neutral composition merely because it currently has only one consumer. A portable-looking renderer such as breadcrumbs belongs in UI; route and resource resolution remain in a shell adapter. Capabilities may depend on lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, and portable UI contracts, but never on application, feature, or product implementations. Add only named capability directories and explicit subpath imports; do not add a capabilities barrel or generic `shared`, `core`, `state`, or `stores` bucket. Use direct imports after moves, without compatibility wrappers. Shared runtime code must not transitively load capability or application implementations. Features use declared public entries when consuming another capability. Source aliases do not enforce package exports, so run the architecture checker. ## Commands Run commands from the repository root using npm workspaces and Turbo: ```sh npm ci --legacy-peer-deps npm run dev:nucleus npm run dev:memotron npm run dev:pointron npm run check:architecture node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs npm run check:apps npm --workspace @21n/account-service run typecheck npm run test npm run lint npm run build:nucleus npm run build:memotron-share ``` Use the Caddy HTTPS hosts and account-service health checks in `AGENTS.md` for local browser work. Run one product server and browser worker at a time when practical. Do not treat compiler success as browser, cloud, native-device, or deployment proof. ## Database changes Regenerate DataFn mappings with the account-service scripts. Generate and commit a forward migration for physical schema changes; never edit an applied migration. Deployment executes the checked-in migration journal. A successful local `datafn:push:local` does not prove that deployment migrations are complete. ## Review and delivery Preserve unrelated checkout changes. Review product configuration and callers before editing. Follow the existing-test and user-facing behavior approval rules in `AGENTS.md`. Keep code free of inline comments and document exported APIs with JSDoc. PR descriptions must identify changed behavior, relevant verification, and unverified environments. # Client ownership and import boundaries Tracked in [TIDY-477](https://linear.app/21n/issue/TIDY-477/enforce-architectural-boundaries-after-client-feature-and-datafn). ## Delivery checklist - [x] Commit the existing reorganization separately from schema, session, and popover fixes. - [x] Move shared focus preferences and sound state into focus ownership, retaining persistence keys. - [x] Remove the composition/session-store cycle by passing fixed end times explicitly. - [x] Move memory upload, search-result, and synced-id helpers out of product implementations. - [x] Supply the graph layout from the product shell. - [x] Move authentication, network authority, connectivity, and logging into non-UI runtime ownership. - [x] Move the active-resource UI store out of DataFn and avatar/icon catalogs into UI ownership and initial app data into configuration. - [x] Remove unused mutation-label helpers from DataFn and depend on the observable-store interface instead of its implementation. - [x] Move shared product contracts and navigation metadata out of product implementations. - [x] Enforce completed boundaries and declare existing public feature entry points. - [x] Pass compiler checks for Nucleum, Pointron, Memotron, and account-service. - [x] Pass seven schema tests, two focus-preferences tests, and three popover tests. - [x] Pass four Nucleum focus browser scenarios with no page errors. - [x] Update the approved existing-test import and mock paths. - [x] Adapt the approved fixed-end-time test setup without changing expected durations; pass 127 tests across all 19 affected unit-test files. - [x] Confirm Playwright discovers all 549 tests in 55 files after import updates. ## Ownership `schema` owns resource definitions. `client/datafn` owns the client storage and sync runtime. `client/runtime` owns browser infrastructure such as account transport, network authority, connectivity, and diagnostic logging. `client/features` owns capability implementations. `client/products` composes those capabilities into product experiences. Client product identity composition lives in `client/config/product.type.ts`; cross-layer product identity lives in `schema/product.type.ts`; declarative navigation metadata lives in `client/config`. `client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, modal orchestration, record presentation, app-specific integrations, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory. ## Enforced rules Run `npm run check:architecture`. CI and the root lint command run the same check. It resolves relative imports, source aliases, dynamic imports, and TypeScript import types in TypeScript and Svelte scripts. - Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition; the top-level shell is the only app-level layer features may consume. Surfaces may compose features; features must never import surfaces. - The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`). - Portable UI cannot directly or transitively import application state, runtime, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state. - Compositions may use elements, actions, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers cannot import compositions. - Shared state cannot directly or transitively import application, feature, or product implementations. - DataFn and runtime files cannot directly import features, products, application composition or shell, portable UI, or shared client state and services. - Composition calculations cannot import the session singleton. - A caller outside a capability must use a source file explicitly listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. The feature entry-point list records the existing public surface, including individual components and type modules; it is not a barrel module. Additions require an explicit contract change. Package exports expose these same paths. Source aliases bypass package exports, which is why the source-level check remains necessary. ## Current architecture contract Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic. `client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively. Consumers import named subpaths such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`; there is no root barrel, `shared`, `core`, generic `state`, or nested generic `stores` bucket. Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary. Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Portable file presentation, resource enums, event contracts, and action identifiers no longer depend on capability implementations. The public feature API is enumerated in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. Each has a static consumer outside its capability. The checker rejects unused public entries and private external imports. This reduces the previous 154 entries by moving shared contracts and infrastructure to their proper owners without introducing barrels or compatibility paths. Registered workspaces declare their production source imports. `@nucleum/client` owns lower-level config and runtime; `@nucleum/shared-state` owns product-independent shared client behavior, application context, command ports, and events; `@nucleum/shell` owns the application shell; `@nucleum/surfaces` owns cross-feature product surfaces; `@21n/ui` owns all portable presentation and visual assets. Source workspaces bundled by an app declare co-hosted workspace requirements as peer dependencies; existing build dependencies remain dependencies. Peers describe the host's source compilation requirements without adding artificial Turbo build cycles. This is not a claim that each source package builds or installs independently. The checker verifies both resolved workspace and external package imports; test and story dependencies are outside this production-source check. The narrow Library now mounts resource panes only after a resource is selected. A dedicated focus-capability test covers the portrait Library in Nucleum and Pointron; a seeded Recents probe verifies visibility before and after reload without page errors. Broader regression results are recorded below separately from the architecture checks. ## Application-state ownership follow-up Product and application context lives in `client/shared-state/app-context/app.store.ts`. Browser/embed environment context lives in `client/runtime/context.store.ts`; persistent UI preference state lives in `client/shared-state/preferences/ui-state`; legacy product-key migration belongs to `client/persistence/migrations`. URL/history and resource navigation live in `client/shell/navigation/navigation.ts`. Product command lookup/execution lives in `client/surfaces/commands/action-runner.ts`; the permanent shared `CommandHost` contract lives in `client/shared-state/commands/command-host.ts` and is installed from `resource-hosts.ts`. Application-wide events live in `client/shared-state/events`. No old methods delegate to the new owners. Reactive account session state lives with the account runtime in `client/runtime/account/account.store.ts`. Authentication persistence, bootstrap, sign-in, sign-out, navigation, and DataFn teardown are coordinated by `client/surfaces/account/account-session.ts`. Deletion confirmation and cleanup orchestration live in `client/surfaces/account/account-deletion.ts`; subscription operations live in `client/surfaces/subscription/subscription.ts`; file conversion, thumbnail generation, signing, and local/remote storage live in `client/shared-state/files/file-upload.ts`. Legacy OAuth initiation belongs to application account composition. The connected offline-status indicator lives with sync settings in `client/surfaces/settings/sync`; shared elements do not read account session state. Application and product shells consume the application-owned indicator directly. Product menu persistence lives beside navigation. Tab and sidebar mutations live beside the application shell; generic UI-state persistence belongs to the preferences capability. Shortcut persistence, matching, hints, and the host contract live in `client/shared-state/shortcuts`; global shortcut execution lives in `client/shell/shortcuts`, and shortcut settings presentation lives in `client/surfaces/settings/shortcuts`. Headless notification state lives in `client/shared-state/notifications`, while connected notification rendering lives in `client/shell/notifications`. Focus owns its scheduled notification queue, and the existing native transport delivers messages. Memory owns its word-count and PDF-overlay DOM actions. The unused Markdown action and empty `@nucleum/cx` workspace are retired, including active aliases and workspace declarations. The former `client/stores`, `client/state`, `client/commands`, and `client/events` directories are retired. App context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts have explicit owners under `client/shared-state`. Runtime environment state belongs to runtime, migration state belongs to persistence, the observable-store implementation belongs to DataFn, and overlay state belongs to the application shell. New state follows semantic ownership and must not recreate a catch-all `stores`, `state`, `shared`, or `core` directory; `client/shared-state` is the single approved shared-state workspace and keeps named owners with no root barrel. ## UI asset and shell consolidation Portable legacy SVG/Rive icons, generated icon mappings, sprite resolution, and spinner components live under `client/ui/icons` and are imported through `@21n/ui/icons/*`. The UI package never imports the product static package; the application supplies asset URL resolution through the UI environment contract. The standalone `@21n/icons` and `@21n/icons-v2` workspaces are retired. Portable illustrations live under `client/ui/illustrations`, and pure product/provider marks live under `client/ui/branding`. The product-aware `SubAtomLogo` adapter remains under `client/application/branding` because it reads product persistence and composes the portable marks. The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired. The concrete layout package is the top-level `client/shell` workspace. All callers use `@nucleum/shell/*`; the `@21n/layout` package, alias, workspace, and compatibility paths are retired. Features may use the shell's explicit navigation, overlay, and shell-presentation surface when participating in application composition, while imports from surfaces or application composition remain forbidden. Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, command, search, and library) live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). Surfaces may compose features, shell, shared state, runtime, and products; features must never import surfaces. This split dissolves the former catch-all role of `client/application`, which retains only the composition root, modal orchestration, record presentation, and app-specific integrations. ### Consolidation verification (2026-09-19) - Architecture enforcement resolves 2,067 source files and 10,946 imports with zero violations; type ownership validates 383 dispositions and 199 unchanged runtime enums. - Nucleum, Memotron, Pointron, and Timear compiler checks complete with zero errors. Their existing warning counts are 379, 302, 308, and 0 respectively. Account-service and Playwright TypeScript checks pass. - The client Vitest project passes 342 assertions across 58 files, the shared project passes 41 assertions across 8 files, and alias-enforcement tests pass 3 assertions. The client project explicitly inlines Testing Library's Svelte packages so component and non-component tests use the same canonical harness. - Playwright discovers 555 tests in 57 files after source-probe paths are updated. This is collection validation; browser workflows, native packaging, cloud integration, deployment, and the complete Playwright suite were not run for this consolidation. - The Memotron share-extension production build, fixed-wait check, legacy-runtime check, and Turbo build-graph dry run pass. Existing Svelte, accessibility, and chunk-size build warnings remain warnings rather than build failures. ## Verification Preserve product gates, navigation destinations, preference resource keys, schemas, and immediate and durable user-visible behavior. Run the Nucleum, Pointron, and Memotron compiler scripts, account-service typecheck, affected existing unit tests, and the Nucleum focus probe. Record existing extension/compiler or test-harness failures separately from regressions. No cloud transport or deployment coverage is implied by the local probe. ## Historical phase verification records The following records describe each phase at its original commit. Their pending-work notes and counts are historical; the current architecture contract above supersedes them. ### Initial local verification record - `npm run check:architecture`: passed; alias, relative, and dynamic forbidden-import negative controls were rejected. - `npm --workspace nucleus-app run typecheck`: 0 errors, 379 warnings. - `npm --workspace pointron-app run check`: 0 errors, 308 warnings. - `npm --workspace memotron-app run check`: 0 errors, 302 warnings. - `npm --workspace @21n/account-service run typecheck`: passed. - Schema tests: 7 passed using the shared Vitest project with coverage disabled. - Focus preference and popover tests: 5 passed using the client Vitest project, coverage disabled, and the existing dependency-inlining workaround for `@testing-library/svelte` and `@testing-library/svelte-core`. - `node apps/e2e-playwright/scripts/probe-review-session.mjs`: start, reload/fullscreen, interval-boundary, and delivered-reset scenarios passed. Evidence: `apps/e2e-playwright/artifacts/review-session-1788782040041`. The first focused Vitest invocation ran the selected tests successfully but inherited repository-wide coverage collection, which encountered existing missing PDF sourcemaps in generated app bundles. It was stopped and rerun with coverage disabled. No existing test configuration was changed. The approved test-path updates and explicit-end-time setup adaptation are complete. All 127 tests across the 19 affected unit-test files pass. Playwright discovers 549 tests in 55 files; this is collection validation, not execution of the full browser suite. Delivery is local only; nothing has been pushed. `npm run lint` passed the architecture and fixed-wait checks. Turbo reported no package lint tasks; it ran only the static asset build dependency, so this is not full source lint coverage. Its generated manifest was restored after validation. ## Component ownership phase - [x] Separate application composition from shared components. - [x] Move Markdown/tag UI to memory and combinations to spaces. - [x] Move shared preferences and cross-layer contracts out of UI directories. - [x] Update source imports, test/mock paths, Storybook callers, aliases, workspace metadata, and public feature entries without compatibility files. - [x] Enforce shared-component dependency direction, including relative and dynamic imports. - [x] Complete scoped compiler, unit, browser, and architecture verification; deliver this phase as a separate local commit. Portable UI receives product behavior through props or narrow hosts and remains independent of application state, runtime infrastructure, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Product-independent Nucleum behavior shared across features or products lives in named subdirectories of `client/capabilities/` and is imported from `@nucleum/capabilities/*`, including command ports and application events; this package must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. `schema/` owns cross-layer contracts, `client/datafn/` owns storage and sync, and `services/account/` owns the backend. Application workflows and the concrete shell live in `client/application/`, including navigation, notification presentation, and shortcut execution under `client/application/shell`; UI-independent infrastructure lives in `client/runtime/`. State is colocated with app context, runtime, preferences, persistence, shell, or feature owners rather than a generic `client/state` directory. See [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md) for the current ownership model, [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md) for contracts, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for maintainer orientation. # Contributor and maintainer orientation As noted in README.md, external contributions are not currently accepted. This guide documents the workflow for maintainers and authorized agents. Start with [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [WARP.md](WARP.md), [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md), and [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md). Confirm the active product in `client/products` and `client/config`. Reuse `@21n/ui/elements` for atomic controls, `@21n/ui/compositions` for portable domain-neutral compound UI, `@21n/ui/actions` for generic DOM behavior, `@21n/ui/icons` for portable icons, `@21n/ui/illustrations` for artwork, and `@21n/ui/branding` for pure visual brand assets. UI-wide platform state and dependency-inversion contracts belong to `@21n/ui/environment` and `@21n/ui/hosts`, not under an individual element. Keep a composition shared when credible future reuse is intentional even if it currently has one consumer. The entire UI package must remain independent of application state, runtime, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state; inject product behavior through props or narrow host contracts. Keep product-aware branding and other connected adapters with application composition. The concrete application shell lives under `client/application/shell`; the generic `client/layout`, `client/branding`, `client/illustrations`, `client/icons`, `client/iconsV2`, `client/commands`, `client/events`, and `client/state` owners are retired. Product-independent app-context, appearance, command, event, file, notification, preference, resource, and shortcut behavior belongs to named `@nucleum/capabilities/*` subpaths, which must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. Connected notification rendering and shortcut execution belong to the shell, while shortcut settings UI belongs under `client/application/settings/shortcuts`. Use repository scripts for setup, compilation, tests, and builds. Run architecture and type-ownership checks for moves, and include a forward migration when generated database mappings change. Do not modify existing tests without the per-file authorization required by AGENTS.md. PRs should describe the user-visible result, ownership changes, checks performed, and limitations. Do not include secrets, local environment files, build output, or unrelated workspace changes. # Repository guide `AGENTS.md` is the governing agent policy. Read it before changes. The current architecture is documented in [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md) and [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md). ## Organization - `schema/`: cross-layer product/resource definitions, wire contracts, and legacy serialization contracts. - `client/datafn/`: client storage, queries, sync, and DataFn resource adapters. - `client/runtime/`: UI-independent auth/account transport, connectivity, logging, native messaging, audio, and inference. - `client/features/`: shared capabilities such as memory, focus, calendar, collections, and spaces. - `client/products/`: product-specific composition, configuration, and integrations. - `client/config/`: client product identity, navigation metadata, and command identifiers. - `client/application/`: commands, account/subscription workflows, settings, mixed-resource presentation, and the concrete shell under `client/application/shell`. - `client/ui/`: the domain-free `@21n/ui` package. Import atomic controls from `@21n/ui/elements`, reusable compound UI from `@21n/ui/compositions`, generic DOM behavior from `@21n/ui/actions`, portable icons from `@21n/ui/icons`, illustrations from `@21n/ui/illustrations`, pure visual brand assets from `@21n/ui/branding`, portable platform state from `@21n/ui/environment`, and host contracts from `@21n/ui/hosts`. - `client/capabilities/`: the product-independent `@nucleum/capabilities` package with named app-context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts owners. - `client/persistence/`: persistence helpers and legacy backup/recovery boundaries. - `services/account/`: AuthFn/DataFn account service, database mappings, lookup integrations, and Node/Worker deployments. - `shared/`: cross-layer utilities and remaining legacy database objects. - `apps/`, `extensions/`: deployable product and extension bundles; `apps/e2e-playwright` owns browser verification. There is no global `client/types` or `shared/types` package. Import contracts from their domain owner. The unused `@nucleum/cx` workspace is retired. ## Composition rules App context does not implement navigation or command execution. The command capability exposes the application port; the application command runner executes product commands. The application shell changes URL/history and owns connected notification rendering plus global shortcut execution. Shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/application/settings/shortcuts`. Application and extension shells install command, overlay, resource, renderer, shortcut, recents, icon-asset, and UI-environment hosts through `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` before mounting consumers. Compositions may use elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers must not depend on compositions. Nothing under `client/ui` may directly or transitively depend on application state, runtime, shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state. Supply connected behavior through props or narrow host contracts and keep the adapter with its application, shell, or feature owner. Product-aware branding is an application adapter over portable brand assets. Do not move a domain-neutral composition merely because it currently has only one consumer. A portable-looking renderer such as breadcrumbs belongs in UI; route and resource resolution remain in a shell adapter. Capabilities may depend on lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, and portable UI contracts, but never on application, feature, or product implementations. Add only named capability directories and explicit subpath imports; do not add a capabilities barrel or generic `shared`, `core`, `state`, or `stores` bucket. Use direct imports after moves, without compatibility wrappers. Shared runtime code must not transitively load capability or application implementations. Features use declared public entries when consuming another capability. Source aliases do not enforce package exports, so run the architecture checker. ## Commands Run commands from the repository root using npm workspaces and Turbo: ```sh npm ci --legacy-peer-deps npm run dev:nucleus npm run dev:memotron npm run dev:pointron npm run check:architecture node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs npm run check:apps npm --workspace @21n/account-service run typecheck npm run test npm run lint npm run build:nucleus npm run build:memotron-share ``` Use the Caddy HTTPS hosts and account-service health checks in `AGENTS.md` for local browser work. Run one product server and browser worker at a time when practical. Do not treat compiler success as browser, cloud, native-device, or deployment proof. ## Database changes Regenerate DataFn mappings with the account-service scripts. Generate and commit a forward migration for physical schema changes; never edit an applied migration. Deployment executes the checked-in migration journal. A successful local `datafn:push:local` does not prove that deployment migrations are complete. ## Review and delivery Preserve unrelated checkout changes. Review product configuration and callers before editing. Follow the existing-test and user-facing behavior approval rules in `AGENTS.md`. Keep code free of inline comments and document exported APIs with JSDoc. PR descriptions must identify changed behavior, relevant verification, and unverified environments. # Client ownership and import boundaries Tracked in [TIDY-477](https://linear.app/21n/issue/TIDY-477/enforce-architectural-boundaries-after-client-feature-and-datafn). ## Delivery checklist - [x] Commit the existing reorganization separately from schema, session, and popover fixes. - [x] Move shared focus preferences and sound state into focus ownership, retaining persistence keys. - [x] Remove the composition/session-store cycle by passing fixed end times explicitly. - [x] Move memory upload, search-result, and synced-id helpers out of product implementations. - [x] Supply the graph layout from the product shell. - [x] Move authentication, network authority, connectivity, and logging into non-UI runtime ownership. - [x] Move the active-resource UI store out of DataFn and avatar/icon catalogs into UI ownership and initial app data into configuration. - [x] Remove unused mutation-label helpers from DataFn and depend on the observable-store interface instead of its implementation. - [x] Move shared product contracts and navigation metadata out of product implementations. - [x] Enforce completed boundaries and declare existing public feature entry points. - [x] Pass compiler checks for Nucleum, Pointron, Memotron, and account-service. - [x] Pass seven schema tests, two focus-preferences tests, and three popover tests. - [x] Pass four Nucleum focus browser scenarios with no page errors. - [x] Update the approved existing-test import and mock paths. - [x] Adapt the approved fixed-end-time test setup without changing expected durations; pass 127 tests across all 19 affected unit-test files. - [x] Confirm Playwright discovers all 549 tests in 55 files after import updates. ## Ownership `schema` owns resource definitions. `client/datafn` owns the client storage and sync runtime. `client/runtime` owns browser infrastructure such as account transport, network authority, connectivity, and diagnostic logging. `client/features` owns capability implementations. `client/products` composes those capabilities into product experiences. Client product identity composition lives in `client/config/product.type.ts`; cross-layer product identity lives in `schema/product.type.ts`; declarative navigation metadata lives in `client/config`. `client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, modal orchestration, record presentation, app-specific integrations, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory. ## Enforced rules Run `npm run check:architecture`. CI and the root lint command run the same check. It resolves relative imports, source aliases, dynamic imports, and TypeScript import types in TypeScript and Svelte scripts. - Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition; the top-level shell is the only app-level layer features may consume. Surfaces may compose features; features must never import surfaces. - The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`). - Portable UI cannot directly or transitively import application state, runtime, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state. - Compositions may use elements, actions, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers cannot import compositions. - Shared state cannot directly or transitively import application, feature, or product implementations. - DataFn and runtime files cannot directly import features, products, application composition or shell, portable UI, or shared client state and services. - Composition calculations cannot import the session singleton. - A caller outside a capability must use a source file explicitly listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. The feature entry-point list records the existing public surface, including individual components and type modules; it is not a barrel module. Additions require an explicit contract change. Package exports expose these same paths. Source aliases bypass package exports, which is why the source-level check remains necessary. ## Current architecture contract Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The portable UI foundation is the single `client/ui` workspace, consumed through `@21n/ui/elements`, `@21n/ui/compositions`, `@21n/ui/actions`, `@21n/ui/icons`, `@21n/ui/illustrations`, `@21n/ui/branding`, `@21n/ui/environment`, and `@21n/ui/hosts`. Compositions may use the other UI layers, while elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts never depend on compositions. The entire package remains independent, directly and transitively, from application state, runtime infrastructure, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Domain-neutral compositions stay in UI when future shared use is intentional, even with one current consumer. Product-connected behavior enters through explicit props or narrow contracts under `client/ui/hosts`, configured from `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` or supplied by the owning shell or feature adapter. Shared state and utilities cannot transitively load application or feature composition at runtime. Explicit type-only edges are excluded from the shared-runtime reachability rule; cross-capability imports remain permitted through declared public entries, so the complete source graph is not claimed to be acyclic. `client/shared-state` is the single `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace. It groups product-independent Nucleum client behavior by semantic owner without turning `client/` into a list of service folders. Shared command ports and application events are shared state because they are consumed across features, products, extensions, and application composition; concrete command execution remains application-owned. Shared state may consume lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, utilities, and portable UI contracts. They may not consume application workflows or shell implementations, user-facing feature implementations, or product composition, directly or transitively. Consumers import named subpaths such as `@nucleum/shared-state/preferences/preferences.store`; there is no root barrel, `shared`, `core`, generic `state`, or nested generic `stores` bucket. Presentation ownership is separate from navigation ownership. Neutral breadcrumbs and scroll containers live in UI. `client/shell/navigation/components/AppBreadcrumbs.svelte` translates application resource and path metadata into structural breadcrumb items and callbacks. Sidebars, tabs, split views, panels, and trails remain in the application shell when they own URL state, resource resolution, product menus, shell events, or other application orchestration. A component moves to UI only when its public contract can be expressed without product or domain vocabulary. Application and extension shells configure permanent overlay, resource-action, panel, shortcut, recents, record-renderer, action-renderer, portable action, shortcut, file, environment, logging, and haptic contracts in `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts`. Configuration runs from base, user, and extension shells before presentation or command execution. Shell and feature adapters provide view-specific props such as keyboard matching, time scales, and address resolution. Shared Markdown display owns portable parsing; memory owns Markdown editing. Deploy to the provider of your choice ```env VITE_PRODUCT={{memotron | pointron | nucleum }} VITE_STATIC_URL=https://cdn.21n.co ``` _Full app deployment including backend will be available soon..._ ## Contributing Due to the current size of our team, we are not accepting external contributions at this time. We appreciate your interest and understanding. ### License This project is licensed under the AGPL-3.0 license. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for details. ### Contact For any questions, security reporting or feedback, please contact us at [hello@21n.co](mailto:hello@21n.co). ❤️ We extend our deepest gratitude to all the [OSS libraries and tools](https://github.com/21nOrg/nucleus/network/dependencies) that made this project possible. ## Code organization Product bundles in `apps/` compose user-facing features from `client/features/`. `client/ui/` is the domain-free, portable `@21n/ui` package: `elements` owns atomic controls, `compositions` owns reusable compound UI such as charts, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, and time controls, `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, `branding` owns pure visual brand assets, and `environment` plus `hosts` provide package-wide integration contracts. Portable UI receives product behavior through props or narrow hosts and remains independent of application state, runtime infrastructure, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Product-independent Nucleum behavior shared across features or products lives in named subdirectories of `client/capabilities/` and is imported from `@nucleum/capabilities/*`, including command ports and application events; this package must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. `schema/` owns cross-layer contracts, `client/datafn/` owns storage and sync, and `services/account/` owns the backend. Application workflows and the concrete shell live in `client/application/`, including navigation, notification presentation, and shortcut execution under `client/application/shell`; UI-independent infrastructure lives in `client/runtime/`. State is colocated with app context, runtime, preferences, persistence, shell, or feature owners rather than a generic `client/state` directory. See [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md) for the current ownership model, [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md) for contracts, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for maintainer orientation. # Contributor and maintainer orientation As noted in README.md, external contributions are not currently accepted. This guide documents the workflow for maintainers and authorized agents. Start with [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [WARP.md](WARP.md), [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md), and [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md). Confirm the active product in `client/products` and `client/config`. Reuse `@21n/ui/elements` for atomic controls, `@21n/ui/compositions` for portable domain-neutral compound UI, `@21n/ui/actions` for generic DOM behavior, `@21n/ui/icons` for portable icons, `@21n/ui/illustrations` for artwork, and `@21n/ui/branding` for pure visual brand assets. UI-wide platform state and dependency-inversion contracts belong to `@21n/ui/environment` and `@21n/ui/hosts`, not under an individual element. Keep a composition shared when credible future reuse is intentional even if it currently has one consumer. The entire UI package must remain independent of application state, runtime, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state; inject product behavior through props or narrow host contracts. Keep product-aware branding and other connected adapters with application composition. The concrete application shell lives under `client/application/shell`; the generic `client/layout`, `client/branding`, `client/illustrations`, `client/icons`, `client/iconsV2`, `client/commands`, `client/events`, and `client/state` owners are retired. Product-independent app-context, appearance, command, event, file, notification, preference, resource, and shortcut behavior belongs to named `@nucleum/capabilities/*` subpaths, which must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. Connected notification rendering and shortcut execution belong to the shell, while shortcut settings UI belongs under `client/application/settings/shortcuts`. Use repository scripts for setup, compilation, tests, and builds. Run architecture and type-ownership checks for moves, and include a forward migration when generated database mappings change. Do not modify existing tests without the per-file authorization required by AGENTS.md. PRs should describe the user-visible result, ownership changes, checks performed, and limitations. Do not include secrets, local environment files, build output, or unrelated workspace changes. # Repository guide `AGENTS.md` is the governing agent policy. Read it before changes. The current architecture is documented in [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md) and [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md). ## Organization - `schema/`: cross-layer product/resource definitions, wire contracts, and legacy serialization contracts. - `client/datafn/`: client storage, queries, sync, and DataFn resource adapters. - `client/runtime/`: UI-independent auth/account transport, connectivity, logging, native messaging, audio, and inference. - `client/features/`: shared capabilities such as memory, focus, calendar, collections, and spaces. - `client/products/`: product-specific composition, configuration, and integrations. - `client/config/`: client product identity, navigation metadata, and command identifiers. - `client/application/`: commands, account/subscription workflows, settings, mixed-resource presentation, and the concrete shell under `client/application/shell`. - `client/ui/`: the domain-free `@21n/ui` package. Import atomic controls from `@21n/ui/elements`, reusable compound UI from `@21n/ui/compositions`, generic DOM behavior from `@21n/ui/actions`, portable icons from `@21n/ui/icons`, illustrations from `@21n/ui/illustrations`, pure visual brand assets from `@21n/ui/branding`, portable platform state from `@21n/ui/environment`, and host contracts from `@21n/ui/hosts`. - `client/capabilities/`: the product-independent `@nucleum/capabilities` package with named app-context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts owners. - `client/persistence/`: persistence helpers and legacy backup/recovery boundaries. - `services/account/`: AuthFn/DataFn account service, database mappings, lookup integrations, and Node/Worker deployments. - `shared/`: cross-layer utilities and remaining legacy database objects. - `apps/`, `extensions/`: deployable product and extension bundles; `apps/e2e-playwright` owns browser verification. There is no global `client/types` or `shared/types` package. Import contracts from their domain owner. Portable UI receives product behavior through props or narrow hosts and remains independent of application state, runtime infrastructure, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state. Product-independent Nucleum behavior shared across features or products lives in named subdirectories of `client/capabilities/` and is imported from `@nucleum/capabilities/*`, including command ports and application events; this package must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. `schema/` owns cross-layer contracts, `client/datafn/` owns storage and sync, and `services/account/` owns the backend. Application workflows and the concrete shell live in `client/application/`, including navigation, notification presentation, and shortcut execution under `client/application/shell`; UI-independent infrastructure lives in `client/runtime/`. State is colocated with app context, runtime, preferences, persistence, shell, or feature owners rather than a generic `client/state` directory. Start with [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [WARP.md](WARP.md), [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md), and [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md). Confirm the active product in `client/products` and `client/config`. Reuse `@21n/ui/elements` for atomic controls, `@21n/ui/compositions` for portable domain-neutral compound UI, `@21n/ui/actions` for generic DOM behavior, `@21n/ui/icons` for portable icons, `@21n/ui/illustrations` for artwork, and `@21n/ui/branding` for pure visual brand assets. UI-wide platform state and dependency-inversion contracts belong to `@21n/ui/environment` and `@21n/ui/hosts`, not under an individual element. Keep a composition shared when credible future reuse is intentional even if it currently has one consumer. The entire UI package must remain independent of application state, runtime, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, and domain state; inject product behavior through props or narrow host contracts. Keep product-aware branding and other connected adapters with application composition. The concrete application shell lives under `client/application/shell`; the generic `client/layout`, `client/branding`, `client/illustrations`, `client/icons`, `client/iconsV2`, `client/commands`, `client/events`, and `client/state` owners are retired. Product-independent app-context, appearance, command, event, file, notification, preference, resource, and shortcut behavior belongs to named `@nucleum/capabilities/*` subpaths, which must not depend on application, feature, or product implementations. Connected notification rendering and shortcut execution belong to the shell, while shortcut settings UI belongs under `client/application/settings/shortcuts`. Use repository scripts for setup, compilation, tests, and builds. Run architecture and type-ownership checks for moves, and include a forward migration when generated database mappings change. The current architecture is documented in [client boundaries](docs/architecture/client-boundaries.md) and [type ownership](docs/architecture/type-ownership.md). ## Organization - `schema/`: cross-layer product/resource definitions, wire contracts, and legacy serialization contracts. - `client/datafn/`: client storage, queries, sync, and DataFn resource adapters. - `client/runtime/`: UI-independent auth/account transport, connectivity, logging, native messaging, audio, and inference. - `client/features/`: shared capabilities such as memory, focus, calendar, collections, and spaces. - `client/products/`: product-specific composition, configuration, and integrations. - `client/config/`: client product identity, navigation metadata, and command identifiers. - `client/application/`: commands, account/subscription workflows, settings, mixed-resource presentation, and the concrete shell under `client/application/shell`. - `client/ui/`: the domain-free `@21n/ui` package. Import atomic controls from `@21n/ui/elements`, reusable compound UI from `@21n/ui/compositions`, generic DOM behavior from `@21n/ui/actions`, portable icons from `@21n/ui/icons`, illustrations from `@21n/ui/illustrations`, pure visual brand assets from `@21n/ui/branding`, portable platform state from `@21n/ui/environment`, and host contracts from `@21n/ui/hosts`. - `client/capabilities/`: the product-independent `@nucleum/capabilities` package with named app-context, appearance, commands, events, files, notifications, preferences, resources, and shortcuts owners. - `client/persistence/`: persistence helpers and legacy backup/recovery boundaries. - `services/account/`: AuthFn/DataFn account service, database mappings, lookup integrations, and Node/Worker deployments. - `shared/`: cross-layer utilities and remaining legacy database objects. - `apps/`, `extensions/`: deployable product and extension bundles; `apps/e2e-playwright` owns browser verification. There is no global `client/types` or `shared/types` package. Import contracts from their domain owner. The unused `@nucleum/cx` workspace is retired. ## Composition rules App context does not implement navigation or command execution. The command capability exposes the application port; the application command runner executes product commands. The application shell changes URL/history and owns connected notification rendering plus global shortcut execution. Shortcut settings presentation belongs under `client/application/settings/shortcuts`. Application and extension shells install command, overlay, resource, renderer, shortcut, recents, icon-asset, and UI-environment hosts through `client/application/composition/resource-hosts.ts` before mounting consumers. Compositions may use elements, actions, icons, illustrations, branding, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers must not depend on compositions. Nothing under `client/ui` may directly or transitively depend on application state, runtime, shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state. Supply connected behavior through props or narrow host contracts and keep the adapter with its application, shell, or feature owner. Product-aware branding is an application adapter over portable brand assets. Do not move a domain-neutral composition merely because it currently has only one consumer. A portable-looking renderer such as breadcrumbs belongs in UI; route and resource resolution remain in a shell adapter. Capabilities may depend on lower-level runtime, DataFn, persistence, schema, and portable UI contracts, but never on application, feature, or product implementations. Add only named capability directories and explicit subpath imports; do not add a capabilities barrel or generic `shared`, `core`, `state`, or `stores` bucket. Use direct imports after moves, without compatibility wrappers. Shared runtime code must not transitively load capability or application implementations. Features use declared public entries when consuming another capability. Source aliases do not enforce package exports, so run the architecture checker. ## Commands Run commands from the repository root using npm workspaces and Turbo: ```sh npm ci --legacy-peer-deps npm run dev:nucleus npm run dev:memotron npm run dev:pointron npm run check:architecture node tools/check/type-ownership.mjs npm run check:apps npm --workspace @21n/account-service run typecheck npm run test npm run lint npm run build:nucleus npm run build:memotron-share ``` Use the Caddy HTTPS hosts and account-service health checks in `AGENTS.md` for local browser work. Client product identity composition lives in `client/config/product.type.ts`; cross-layer product identity lives in `schema/product.type.ts`; declarative navigation metadata lives in `client/config`. `client/ui` is the permanent domain-free `@21n/ui` package. `elements` owns atomic controls and UI-only types. `compositions` owns domain-neutral compound UI intended for present or future reuse, including charts, maps, breadcrumbs, nested lists, search controls, file presentation, keyboard listeners, duration inputs, scroll containers, and time selectors. `actions` owns generic DOM behavior, `icons` owns portable icon assets and rendering, `illustrations` owns portable artwork, and `branding` owns pure visual brand assets. Package-wide portable platform state belongs to `environment`, while dependency-inversion contracts shared across controls and compositions belong to `hosts`. A single current consumer does not make a composition feature-owned. `client/shell` (`@nucleum/shell`) owns the concrete product shell: navigation, panels, split views, tabs, trails, overlays, modal chrome, and the extension-support layers. `client/surfaces` (`@nucleum/surfaces`) owns cross-feature product surfaces: account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, the command surface (`commandBar`, `commands`, `search`), and `library` resource browsing. `client/application` retains the composition root (`composition/resource-hosts.ts`, `composition/shortcuts.config.ts`), the base/user application layers, modal orchestration, record presentation, app-specific integrations, and product-aware branding adapters. Markdown editing and tags belong to memory; combinations belong to spaces. Product-independent shared client behavior lives in the `@nucleum/shared-state` workspace under explicit `app-context`, `appearance`, `commands`, `events`, `files`, `notifications`, `preferences`, `product`, `resources`, and `shortcuts` owners. Cross-layer billing contracts live in `schema/account`. Keyboard and interaction-mode contracts live in `client/ui/elements/keyboard`; panel and error presentation contracts live in their capability owners. See [type ownership](type-ownership.md) for the complete inventory. ## Enforced rules Run `npm run check:architecture`. CI and the root lint command run the same check. It resolves relative imports, source aliases, dynamic imports, and TypeScript import types in TypeScript and Svelte scripts. - Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition; the top-level shell is the only app-level layer features may consume. Surfaces may compose features; features must never import surfaces. - The application shell is acyclic: `client/shell` must not import application, surfaces, or products, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters only through `@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome (brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status, capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props wired by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`). - Portable UI cannot directly or transitively import application state, runtime, the application shell, products, features, DataFn, persistence, schema, or domain state. - Compositions may use elements, actions, environment, and hosts; those lower UI layers cannot import compositions. - Shared state cannot directly or transitively import application, feature, or product implementations. - DataFn and runtime files cannot directly import features, products, application composition or shell, portable UI, or shared client state and services. - Composition calculations cannot import the session singleton. - A caller outside a capability must use a source file explicitly listed in `tools/check/feature-entrypoints.json`. The feature entry-point list records the existing public surface, including individual components and type modules; it is not a barrel module. Additions require an explicit contract change. Package exports expose these same paths. Source aliases bypass package exports, which is why the source-level check remains necessary. ## Current architecture contract Features cannot import product implementations, surfaces, or application composition. The application shell is the top-level `client/shell` workspace (`@nucleum/shell`), the only app-level layer features may consume. Cross-feature product surfaces live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`); surfaces may compose features, while features never import surfaces. The UI package never imports the product static package; the application supplies asset URL resolution through the UI environment contract. The product-aware `SubAtomLogo` adapter remains under `client/application/branding` because it reads product persistence and composes the portable marks. The portable external-logo renderer owns its provider identifiers and accepts integration configuration through props instead of importing account runtime state. The standalone `@21n/illustrations` and `@21n/branding` workspaces and aliases are retired. The concrete layout package is the top-level `client/shell` workspace. All callers use `@nucleum/shell/*`; the `@21n/layout` package, alias, workspace, and compatibility paths are retired. Features may use the shell's explicit navigation, overlay, and shell-presentation surface when participating in application composition, while imports from surfaces or application composition remain forbidden. Cross-feature product surfaces (account, subscription, onboarding, help, settings, command, search, and library) live in the top-level `client/surfaces` workspace (`@nucleum/surfaces`). Surfaces may compose features, shell, shared state, runtime, and products; features must never import surfaces. # `client/shell` — application shell: arrangement and navigation (`@nucleum/shell`)

Charter: how the app is arranged and moved through, independent of what content
fills it. Pure "where things go and how you move", never "what a screen does".

## Owners

`navigation` (URL/history, resource navigation), `topNav`, `bottomNav`,
`leftPanel`, `rightPanel`, `trail`, `layers` (theme, sync, metadata, embed,
analytics, cache, support chrome), `overlays`, `modal`, `paint` (page and
resource resolvers fed through the shared-state action renderer), `split views`,
`tabs`, `sync` and `notifications` chrome.

## Belongs here

Anything that owns URL state, panel arrangement, tab/sidebar behavior, product
menus, or shell events. If removing it would not change what any single screen
does, only how screens are framed and reached, it belongs here.

## Not here

- Domain screens and workflows (account, library, settings, command) ->
  `surfaces/`.
- Portable domain-free UI -> `ui/`.
- Content capabilities -> `features/`.
- Application composition layers that wire the running product together
  (base/user layers, the action `ComponentResolver`, `AppLoadingView`, and the
  settings action map) -> `application/`.

## Dependency direction (enforced)

Shell is acyclic: it must not import `application/`, `surfaces/`, or
`products/`, directly or transitively. Product navigation config enters through
`@nucleum/shared-state/product/product-config-host`; concrete chrome
(brand/logo, account avatar, search input, bulk-edit bar, offline status,
capture, profile section) enters through optional Svelte snippet props provided
by the application chrome adapters (`client/application/chrome/`).

## Junk-drawer test

A shell component may read navigation and shell state, but it must not contain a
